A time of wars, migrations and new states in southern Africa, at its height from the 1810s to the 1840s. "Mfecane" is a Nguni word, often translated as "the crushing"; Sotho speakers call it the Difaqane.

The old story puts the rise of the Zulu kingdom under Shaka at its centre. Defeated groups fled, attacked their neighbours and set off a chain of movements across the region:

  • Mzilikazi led the Ndebele onto the highveld and later north into what is now Zimbabwe.
  • Moshoeshoe gathered refugees on a mountain stronghold and built the Basotho kingdom, the root of Lesotho.
  • Sebetwane's Kololo went north and took over the Lozi kingdom on the upper Zambezi.
  • Zwangendaba's Nguni followers crossed the Zambezi in 1835 and became the Ngoni of Malawi and Tanzania.

Historians now argue over this story. Drought, competition for the ivory and slave trade through Delagoa Bay, and raids for labour from the Cape Colony also drove the violence. The old death tolls of one or two million are doubted. What is agreed is that the period left behind new kingdoms and peoples, and emptied some land that Boer trekkers soon moved into.
sum: A time of wars, migrations and new states in southern Africa, at its height from the 1810s to the 1840s. "Mfecane" is a Nguni word, often translated as "the crushing"; Sotho speakers call it the Difaqane.
